questions.question_es: ¿Cuál es el objetivo principal de la Integración Continua (CI)?
questions.question_en: What is the primary goal of Continuous Integration (CI)?
options_es: Que los desarrolladores integren sus cambios en la rama principal frecuentemente (varias veces al día), verificando cada integración con un build y tests automatizados
Desplegar automáticamente a producción cada commit sin revisión
Eliminar la necesidad de escribir tests
options_en: Having developers integrate their changes into the main branch frequently (several times a day), verifying each integration with an automated build and tests
Automatically deploying every commit to production with no review
Eliminating the need to write tests
questions.explanation_es: CI busca detectar problemas de integración temprano, integrando cambios pequeños y frecuentes a una rama compartida, cada uno validado automáticamente por build + tests.
questions.explanation_en: CI aims to catch integration problems early by integrating small, frequent changes into a shared branch, each automatically validated by a build + tests.
questions.source: Fowler, M. — Continuous Integration (martinfowler.com); Humble & Farley — Continuous Delivery

questions.question_es: Un pipeline de CI que tarda más de una hora en dar feedback sobre un commit sigue considerándose una buena práctica siempre que finalmente se ejecute.
questions.question_en: A CI pipeline that takes more than an hour to give feedback on a commit is still considered good practice as long as it eventually runs.
questions.explanation_es: Una práctica clave de CI es la retroalimentación RÁPIDA; pipelines lentos desalientan la integración frecuente y retrasan la detección de errores. Se recomienda optimizar (paralelizar, cachear, tests rápidos primero) para mantener ciclos cortos.
questions.explanation_en: A key CI practice is FAST feedback; slow pipelines discourage frequent integration and delay error detection. Optimizing (parallelizing, caching, fast tests first) is recommended to keep cycles short.
questions.source: Humble & Farley — Continuous Delivery, cap. 3 (Continuous Integration)

questions.question_es: En un workflow de GitHub Actions, ¿qué palabra clave define las condiciones (eventos) que disparan la ejecución del workflow?
questions.question_en: In a GitHub Actions workflow, which keyword defines the conditions (events) that trigger the workflow's execution?
questions.explanation_es: La clave `on` en el YAML del workflow especifica los eventos que lo disparan (p.ej. `push`, `pull_request`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`).
questions.explanation_en: The `on` key in the workflow YAML specifies the events that trigger it (e.g. `push`, `pull_request`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`).
questions.source: GitHub Docs — Workflow syntax for GitHub Actions (on)

questions.question_es: ¿Cuál es la diferencia clave entre Continuous Delivery y Continuous Deployment?
questions.question_en: What is the key difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
options_es: En Continuous Delivery cada cambio que pasa las pruebas queda listo para desplegarse pero requiere una aprobación/acción manual final; en Continuous Deployment ese despliegue a producción ocurre automáticamente sin intervención humana
Continuous Deployment no usa control de versiones
Continuous Delivery solo aplica a mobile apps
options_en: In Continuous Delivery every change that passes tests is ready to deploy but requires a final manual approval/action; in Continuous Deployment that deploy to production happens automatically with no human intervention
Continuous Deployment doesn't use version control
Continuous Delivery only applies to mobile apps
questions.explanation_es: Ambos comparten la base de tener el software siempre en estado desplegable; la diferencia es el último paso: Delivery deja el despliegue como decisión manual, Deployment automatiza también ese último paso a producción.
questions.explanation_en: Both share the foundation of keeping software always in a deployable state; the difference is the last step: Delivery leaves deployment as a manual decision, Deployment also automates that last step to production.
questions.source: Humble & Farley — Continuous Delivery, cap. 1 (Continuous Delivery vs Deployment)

questions.question_es: Una estrategia de despliegue "blue-green" mantiene dos entornos de producción idénticos, y el corte de tráfico de uno a otro permite un rollback casi instantáneo si algo falla.
questions.question_en: A "blue-green" deployment strategy keeps two identical production environments, and switching traffic from one to the other allows near-instant rollback if something fails.
questions.explanation_es: En blue-green, "blue" es el entorno activo y "green" el nuevo; tras validar green, el router/balanceador redirige el tráfico. Si aparecen problemas, basta con revertir el tráfico al entorno "blue" anterior, que sigue intacto.
questions.explanation_en: In blue-green, "blue" is the active environment and "green" is the new one; after validating green, the router/load balancer redirects traffic. If problems appear, traffic can simply be reverted to the previous "blue" environment, which remains intact.
questions.source: Humble & Farley — Continuous Delivery, cap. 10 (Blue-Green Deployment)

questions.question_es: Según la "pirámide de pruebas" (test pyramid), ¿qué tipo de test debería tener MAYOR cantidad en un pipeline de CI bien balanceado?
questions.question_en: According to the "test pyramid", which type of test should have the LARGEST quantity in a well-balanced CI pipeline?
options_es: Tests end-to-end (E2E) a través de la UI
questions.explanation_es: La pirámide de pruebas de Cohn recomienda una base amplia de tests unitarios (rápidos, baratos, aislados), una capa media de tests de integración, y pocos tests E2E en la cima (lentos, frágiles, costosos de mantener).
questions.explanation_en: Cohn's test pyramid recommends a broad base of unit tests (fast, cheap, isolated), a middle layer of integration tests, and few E2E tests at the top (slow, brittle, costly to maintain).
questions.source: Cohn, M. — Succeeding with Agile (Test Pyramid); Fowler, M. — TestPyramid (martinfowler.com)
